summary: The quote latency degradation in INC-006 is best explained by H1 (confidence 0.72, medium): an unplanned redis-cache primary failure at 13:22:10Z promoted an EMPTY, still-resyncing replica at 13:22:52Z, which caused a cold-cache miss storm in market-data-service (289 quote rebuilds from the exchange feed, 1.0-8.7s each, from 13:22:25Z) and drove pricing-engine quote computation past its deadline (first error 13:23:57Z, p99 stepping from ~60ms to ~2.2s). The mechanism chain is verified and monotonic across logs (failover -> empty-replica promotion -> miss storm -> first deadline error within 107s), sits inside the 13:16-13:24Z onset bracket, and every tested alternative is contradicted: no deployment or config change on the quote path (including redis-cache itself), pricing-engine CPU flat, and the api-gateway clean. The main residual weakness is that the "market-data-service slow -> pricing-engine deadlines" hop rests on logs, not metrics, because all redis-cache and market-data-service metrics were permanently unavailable (circuit_open), and the "shared" blast radius is only weak-positive from the sparse off-path consumer logs.

ranked_hypotheses.title: redis-cache primary failure promoted an EMPTY replica → cold-cache storm → market-data-service slow → pricing-engine quote deadlines
ranked_hypotheses.statement: At 13:22:10Z the redis-cache primary redis-cache-2 failed three consecutive PING health checks and was marked down; failover promoted replica redis-cache-3, which was still resyncing and therefore EMPTY (13:22:52Z). redis-cache is the only shared=true node on the quote path, consumed as kind='cache' by both market-data-service and pricing-engine (F3, F28). With the dataset gone, market-data-service missed quote keys and rebuilt each from the exchange feed snapshot (1034–8748ms per key, 289 WARNs from 13:22:25Z), and its own served p50 rose to 269–372ms across 13:25–13:47Z (F21). pricing-engine's direct downstream http dependency (market-data-service) therefore answered slowly, pushing quote computation past its deadline: the only ERROR signature on pricing-engine is 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms', first at 13:23:57Z. pricing-engine p99 stepped from ~60ms to ~2.2s and error rate from ~0.2% to ~4% in the 13:20Z bucket, sustained through mid-afternoon. Later reconnect storms and full resyncs (13:28–13:40Z) are sustainers, not the onset mechanism. The chain is now a monotonic, verified 107-second log sequence (failover → empty-replica promotion → miss storm → first deadline error) sitting inside the 13:16–13:24Z onset bracket.

causal_chain.claim: redis-cache primary redis-cache-2 fails 3 consecutive PING health checks and is marked down at 13:22:10Z; pre-incident redis-cache logs (11:00–12:30Z, and persistence/health-normal lines through 13:18:40Z) show no failover or reconnect activity, so this is a new event, not a pre-existing condition
Failover promotes replica redis-cache-3 at 13:22:52Z with an explicitly EMPTY, still-resyncing dataset — the only hit-rate-adjacent statement the redis-cache log source ever emits

Because redis-cache is the shared cache node on the quote path (consumed by both market-data-service and pricing-engine), the empty dataset makes market-data-service miss quote keys and rebuild each from the exchange feed snapshot, 1034–8748ms per key, starting 13:22:25Z — ~15s after the promotion and ~92s before pricing-engine's first deadline error

market-data-service is itself measurably slow during the incident (served p50 269–372ms vs ~60ms pre-onset p99 baseline); this is log-derived and only sampled from 13:25:19Z, so it confirms slowness but does not independently establish it preceded the first deadline error

Slowed market-data-service responses push pricing-engine quote computation past its deadline; the only pricing-engine ERROR signature is 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms', first at 13:23:57Z (192 events, up to 8456ms individual)
pricing-engine p99 and error_rate step together in the 13:20:00Z bucket (~60ms→1143ms avg/2227ms max; ~0.2%→2.71%), consistent with an onset in 13:17–13:24Z that contains the 13:22:10Z failover

Continued unstable/recovering primary sustains the degradation: client reconnect storms at 13:30:20Z (15048 conns/10s) and 13:40:15Z (92851 conns/10s) and two full resyncs (13:28:42Z, 13:35:26Z) — these postdate the onset and act as sustainers, not the trigger

The origin is not any release or config change: redis-cache had zero deployments (F26) and zero config/flag changes (F27) across the window, and no redis-cache consumer received a release either (F30), so the failover is an infrastructure event rather than a change-triggered one

assumptions: The mechanistic steps are inferred, not measured: every redis-cache and market-data-service metric returned circuit_open/503 permanently (F20, F23, F24), so 'market-data-service actually slow → pricing-engine deadlines' and 'empty replica → miss storm' rest on log timelines and log-derived p50, not on metric series

The 13:22:10Z failover is treated as a spontaneous primary failure; the upstream cause of the three PING timeouts (memory-limit OOM, node/drain event, network) is unobserved — the precursor search timed out and no precedent for an external precursor exists (F31)

Whether the dataset was empty due to the promotion itself rather than eviction/memory-pressure/TTL is unestablished: memory_pct and evicted_keys were never obtained (F24). If eviction were the cause the sub-category would shift to resource_exhaustion; the empty-replica promotion WARN (F39) makes promotion the parsimonious reading
Onset is bracketed only to the 240s bucket 13:16–13:20Z (F8), so tight precedence of the 13:22:10Z failover over the degraded bucket is inferential, mitigated by the 13:23:57Z first error log

The blast-radius framing is weakened, not confirmed: neither off-path redis-cache consumer (auth-service, portfolio-service) showed any error/reconnect/hit-miss signature at ~13:22Z (F32/F33/F34/F37), but their log volume is so sparse (3–4 lines per 20 min, F36) that a brief or low-rate off-path anomaly cannot be excluded. An alternative reading is that only the quote-path keys (quote:*) were cold/empty after promotion while other consumers' working sets survived — same origin, narrower blast radius

The degraded pause affects pricing-engine chiefly through market-data-service; the second path (pricing-engine→redis-cache direct, and market-data-service→exchange-gateway) is not separately evidenced

ranked_hypotheses.title: pricing-engine capacity saturation under an unmeasured traffic/load surge at market-open-style volumes
ranked_hypotheses.statement: pricing-engine's provisioned capacity was exceeded by a load surge on the quote path, so its own quote computation queues and inflates to 2–3s; the 'market-data-service took <n>ms' deadline-exceeded errors are a secondary artifact of pricing-engine being time-starved rather than of market-data-service genuinely answering slowly. Mirrors historical precedent HIST-113 (record market-open volume exceeded provisioned capacity). No fault change on the quote path is required, consistent with zero deployments for pricing-engine/market-data-service/redis-cache on 2026-04-09.

causal_chain.claim: Traffic on the quote path rises past provisioned capacity at ~13:20Z
pricing-engine work queues, so its own compute time inflates and its downstream calls appear to exceed deadlines
p99 steps to ~2.2s and error rate to ~4% in the 13:20Z bucket
'market-data-service took <n>ms' deadline messages are generated as pricing-engine exhausts its deadline budget

assumptions: An unmeasured traffic surge occurred at ~13:20Z; pricing-engine and market-data-service request_rate for 12:30–14:00Z both failed circuit_open, so flat-vs-rising was never tested and is now permanently unobtainable (F23)
Queueing could occur without CPU saturation, so flat cpu_pct does not by itself refute the hypothesis
The step-change (not gradual ramp) in F7 is atypical for organic load growth

ranked_hypotheses.title: auth-service v7.2.0 session-cookie hardening (dep-5604) degrades a shared component and surfaces as quote latency
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The only recorded change in the window, dep-5604 (auth-service v7.2.0, SameSite=strict session-cookie hardening, 11:30Z, live, not rolled back), is the trigger: stricter cookies force session invalidation and reconnect/re-auth churn that degrades a shared component (e.g. redis-cache or the connection fabric), which then appears as quote latency. The reporter's 'no releases to pricing today' would be consistent with this.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5604 lands at 11:30:00Z with SameSite=strict session cookies, with no config changes anywhere and no rollback
Stricter cookies invalidate sessions and drive re-auth/reconnect churn
The churn degrades a shared component or the connection fabric and raises quote-path latency
pricing-engine p99 and error rate step and deadline-exceeded alerts fire

assumptions: auth-service has an indirect path to the quote path that the depth-2 graph did not capture
Cookie churn can cause redis-cache dataset loss
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Fails on timing, topology, mechanism and blast radius. dep-5604 is ~1h50m before the 13:20–13:24Z step-change with a long quiet gap and no intermediate degradation (F6, F17); the step is sharp, not a gradual creep from 11:30Z (F7). auth-service is off the depth-2 quote path (F3, F6) and redis-cache logs were clean 11:00–12:30Z, so no shared-component degradation existed to attribute to it (F19, F41). No config changes were recorded anywhere (F2/F27) and no redis-cache consumer received a release in the window (F30). auth-service itself is demonstrably healthy through the incident: zero WARN/ERROR in 13:15–13:35Z with 'connection pool stats: healthy' at 13:18:39Z and a normal p50 cadence (F32, F34, F35, F36). No mechanism links SameSite cookie hardening to a redis primary PING-timeout failure at 13:22:10Z.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Quote latency is a client/gateway-side artifact, not pricing-engine server time
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Trading-screen or api-gateway connection handling adds the 2–3s and the pricing-engine alerts are a misattribution; pricing-engine's server-side p99/error-rate steps could be amplified by client-side retry storms rather than reflecting real server compute latency.

causal_chain.claim: Front-end/gateway path adds latency to quote loading
Client retries amplify perceived latency and load
pricing-engine is alerted, though its own signals may be secondary

assumptions: Client-side latency is not instrumented
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: api-gateway logs are essentially clean across the incident (F18: only a benign slow /internal/metrics and a 38ms NTP resync WARN, no independent anomaly or loader signal). pricing-engine's own server-side p99 (F7) and error rate (F10) step in its own metrics, its own ERROR logs (F9) name a server-side dependency with a specific downstream attribution, and market-data-service's own log-derived p50 is elevated (F21). All evidence points to a server-side dependency path, not a client artifact.

facts.statement: redis-cache primary redis-cache-2 was marked down at 2026-04-09T13:22:10Z after three consecutive PING timeouts, and at 13:22:52Z replica redis-cache-3 was promoted with an explicitly EMPTY dataset ('replica was resyncing').

market-data-service logged a cache-miss storm reading quotes from redis-cache: 289 WARNs of pattern 'cache miss storm: quote:<n> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot', first seen 2026-04-09T13:22:25Z with rebuilds of 1034-8748ms.

pricing-engine's only ERROR signature in 12:00-14:59Z is 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms' - 192 matched entries from 13:23:57Z to 14:58:47Z, with individual cases up to 8456ms.

pricing-engine p99 latency stepped from a stable ~60ms (13:16Z bucket avg 60.33/max 62.93) to avg 1143.04/max 2227.82ms in the 13:20:00Z bucket, sustaining ~1.9-2.3s; error rate stepped in the same bucket from ~0.18-0.24% to 2.71% (max 4.23), then ~4% sustained.

redis-cache is the only node flagged shared=true on the quote path, consumed as kind='cache' by both market-data-service and pricing-engine (and also by auth-service and portfolio-service, which sit on disjoint api-gateway branches).

No deployment was recorded on the quote path in the incident window: the only deployment in 11:00-14:00Z anywhere was dep-5604 (auth-service v7.2.0, 11:30Z, live, not rolled back), and auth-service is not an upstream caller or downstream dependency of pricing-engine; market-data-service had zero deployments 06:00-14:59Z, redis-cache zero deployments on 2026-04-09, and order-service/portfolio-service zero in 12:00-14:59Z.
No config changes were recorded for any service in 11:00-14:00Z, and redis-cache specifically had zero config/flag changes in 12:00-14:00Z.
pricing-engine CPU was NOT elevated: cpu_pct stayed flat at ~38.96-40.59% avg (max 44.48) across all buckets 12:00-14:59Z, including the onset bucket.

api-gateway logs were essentially clean across the incident (only a 12:33:24Z slow /internal/metrics request and a 13:39:42Z 38ms NTP resync WARN), showing no independent anomaly or loader signal at the gateway layer.

market-data-service's own log-derived serving p50 was elevated during the incident: 364ms (13:25:19Z), 269ms (13:38:45Z), 372ms (13:47:18Z) - but all three samples postdate the first pricing-engine deadline error at 13:23:57Z.

Pre-incident redis-cache logs (11:00-12:30Z, and up to the last pre-failover line at 13:18:40Z) show no failover, error, or reconnect activity, and no failover/keyspace/hit wording appears before 13:22:10Z.

redis-cache later showed a reconnect storm ('15048 new connections in 10s' at 13:30:20Z, '92851 new connections in 10s' at 13:40:15Z) and two full resyncs (13:28:42Z, 13:35:26Z) - all of which postdate the first deadline error and so are sustainers, not the onset.

The two off-quote-path redis-cache consumers showed no incident-correlated signature: auth-service and portfolio-service produced zero WARN/ERROR lines in 13:15-13:35Z, and across 12:00-14:59Z their only WARNs were pre-onset connection-reset retries, a deprecated TLS cipher, and NTP resyncs - none mentioning redis-cache, cache miss, or failover. portfolio-service reported 'health check ok' at 13:22:32Z, 22s after the failover.

All redis-cache and market-data-service metric queries (redis-cache cache_hit_rate, command_latency_ms, memory_pct, evicted_keys; pricing-engine and market-data-service request_rate; market-data-service latency_p99_ms) returned error type 'circuit_open' and remained unavailable, so the H1-vs-H2 request_rate discriminator and the hit-rate-collapse mechanism could not be measured.

The redis-cache log source emits no cache_hit_rate/keyspace/hit/miss wording (all keyword filters returned total_matched=0); its complete 13:20-13:30Z logset is only 4 entries (primary-down ERROR, empty-replica promotion WARN, background-save INFO, full-resync WARN).

Historical precedent HIST-107 ('Cold cache storm after redis failover', redis-cache + market-data-service, root cause 'Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica', infrastructure_failure) matches the 13:22Z mechanism and services; no precedent for an external precursor to a redis primary failure was returned.

assumptions: The mechanistic hops are inferred, not measured: because every redis-cache and market-data-service metric returned circuit_open (F20, F23, F24), the statements 'empty replica -> miss storm' and 'market-data-service actually slow -> pricing-engine deadlines' rest on log timelines and log-derived p50 rather than metric series.

The 13:22:10Z failover is treated as a spontaneous primary failure; the upstream cause of the three PING timeouts (memory-limit OOM, node/drain event, network) is unobserved - the precursor search timed out (gap).

Whether the dataset was empty because of the promotion itself rather than eviction/memory-pressure/TTL is unestablished: memory_pct and evicted_keys were never obtained (F24). If eviction were the cause the sub-category would shift toward resource_exhaustion; the explicit empty-replica promotion WARN (F39) makes promotion the parsimonious reading.

Onset is bracketed only to the 240s bucket 13:16-13:20Z / 13:16-13:24Z (F8), so tight precedence of the 13:22:10Z failover over the first degraded metric bucket is inferential, mitigated by the 13:23:57Z first error log and the 13:22:25Z miss storm.

The 'shared blast radius' framing is weakened, not confirmed: the two off-path redis-cache consumers showed no error signature (F32/F33/F34/F37) but their log volume is so sparse (3-4 lines per 20 min) that a brief or low-rate anomaly cannot be excluded; an alternative reading is that only quote:* keys were cold after promotion - same origin, narrower blast radius.

H2 (capacity saturation / load surge) remains active-but-unsupported: it is contradicted by the one obtainable metric (flat CPU, F11) and by the step shape (F7), but its discriminator (request_rate flat vs rising) is permanently unobtainable (F23), so the conclusion is a confidence cap on H2 rather than a direct refutation.

The second path (pricing-engine -> redis-cache direct, and market-data-service -> exchange-gateway) is not separately evidenced; the degradation is assumed to reach pricing-engine chiefly through market-data-service.
Statistical confidence of the off-path 'clean absence' and of the log-derived p50 figures is low given the very small number of log lines sampled.

timeline.event: Last clean redis-cache baseline entries: deprecated-TLS-cipher WARN and (12:21:21Z) slow /internal/metrics WARN; no failover, error, or reconnect activity anywhere in 11:00-13:18:40Z.

Only deployment in the 11:00-14:00Z window: dep-5604, auth-service v7.2.0 SameSite=strict session-cookie hardening; auth-service is off the quote path (depth-2 graph) - timing and topology do not align with onset.
pricing-engine p99 still stable at ~60ms (bucket avg 60.33, max 62.93); metric bucket resolution is 240s, so onset lies between this bucket and the next.
Last pre-failover redis-cache log line ('background saving terminated with success'); cache healthy-normal immediately before the failure.
redis-cache primary redis-cache-2 marked down after 3 consecutive PING timeouts (unplanned failover begins on the shared cache node).
market-data-service begins a cache-miss storm: 289 WARNs 'cache miss storm: quote:<n> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot', rebuilds 1034-8748ms.
Off-path consumer portfolio-service logs 'health check ok' 22s after the failover, showing no visible degradation on the disjoint api-gateway branch.
WARN: replica redis-cache-3 promoted to primary with an EMPTY dataset ('replica was resyncing') - the cold-cache condition becomes explicit.
First customer-visible error: pricing-engine ERROR 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms' - 107s after the failover.

pricing-engine onset bucket (13:20:00Z bucket): p99 avg 1143ms / max 2228ms and error rate 2.71% already registered, consistent with onset partway through the 4-minute bucket; CPU stays flat (~39.98%).
First of three market-data-service log-derived p50 samples confirming the neighbour was slow: p50=364ms (then 269ms at 13:38:45Z, 372ms at 13:47:18Z) - all postdate the first deadline error by ~82s.

MASTER <-> REPLICA full resync events begin (13:28:42Z, 13:35:26Z); redis-cache client reconnect storm follows: 15048 new connections in 10s (13:30:20Z), 92851 in 10s (13:40:15Z) - sustainers after onset.
Last market-data-service deadline-exceeded ERROR recorded on pricing-engine; p99 decays toward ~1.16s but remains elevated.

recommended_actions.action: Treat the redis-cache failover as the live fault: verify redis-cache-3 is fully synced with the expected dataset size and that no further primary-down/health-check ERRORs are firing (redis-cache log ERROR/WARN 'failed health check' and 'promoting replica' patterns), and if the promoted node is still short of data, fail back to a fully synced node or force a controlled repromotion.
recommended_actions.rationale: H1 is the accepted origin (0.72): the primary was marked down at 13:22:10Z and the promoted replica was explicitly EMPTY (F13/F39); recovery of a fully populated primary is the direct mitigation for the cold-cache miss storm driving the deadlines.

recommended_actions.action: Warm the quote path: pre-populate quote:* keys in redis-cache from the exchange feed snapshot for the keys market-data-service is rebuilding, so the 1034-8748ms per-key rebuild cost stops being paid on the request path.
recommended_actions.rationale: The 289 rebuild events from the exchange feed snapshot (F14) and the empty promoted dataset (F39) mean every quote key miss is being rebuilt synchronously; warming removes the dominant added latency while data is restored.

recommended_actions.action: Watch pricing-engine p99 (baseline ~60ms, current ~2.2s) and the 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms' ERROR rate as the recovery signal; declare recovery when the ERROR signature stops and p99 returns near baseline for two consecutive buckets.
recommended_actions.rationale: F7, F9 and F10 are the verified, still-available signals for this incident; the deadline-exceeded ERROR pattern is the only ERROR signature on pricing-engine and it tracks the cold cache.

recommended_actions.action: Restore the metric data sources: jointly investigate why query_metrics returned circuit_open ('query_metrics failed 3 times in a row') for all redis-cache and market-data-service metrics during the incident, then re-query redis-cache cache_hit_rate/command_latency_ms/memory_pct/evicted_keys and market-data-service latency_p99_ms to quantitatively confirm the hit-rate collapse and rule out an eviction/memory-pressure cause.
recommended_actions.rationale: F20/F23/F24 mean the central mechanism is log-inferred; memory_pct vs evicted_keys is the unmeasured discriminator between the promotion (infrastructure_failure) and eviction (resource_exhaustion) sub-categories, and the metric source failure is itself a reliability defect that crippled this investigation.

recommended_actions.action: Verify the fix end-to-end: confirm redis-cache has no repeat primary failure or empty-dataset promotion, confirm market-data-service cache-miss storm WARNs stop, and confirm pricing-engine p99/error_rate return to baseline; also confirm no further reconnect/full-resync storms (13:28-13:40Z events).
recommended_actions.rationale: The sustainer events (F16: reconnect storms, two full resyncs) must clear before the incident can be closed, and their clearance is directly observable in the redis-cache logs.

recommended_actions.action: Determine why an empty/ still-resyncing replica was eligible for promotion (failover policy / min-replicas-to-write / replica sync state check) and require a promotion precondition that a replica reports fully synced before it can take over; add a warm-up/data-health gate for the promoted node.
recommended_actions.rationale: The empty-replica promotion WARN (F39/F13) is the direct cause of the cold-cache storm; HIST-107 (F31/F5) shows the same mechanism has recurred, so the failover guard is the systemic prevention.

recommended_actions.action: Close the observability gaps that blocked this investigation: make redis-cache emit/export a cache_hit_rate and dataset-size signal (its log source has no hit/miss/keyspace wording at all - F38/F40/F43), ensure market-data-service and redis-cache metric backends do not circuit-open without degrading gracefully, and give the cache-miss/rebuild path a metric (count and duration) rather than only logs.
recommended_actions.rationale: The report's confidence is capped by permanently unavailable metrics (F20/F23/F24) and a redis-cache log source with no hit-rate series (F38/F43); without these, the next recurrence cannot be confirmed faster than this one.

recommended_actions.action: Add a precursor signal for redis-cache primary failures: alert on PING-timeout/health-check failures and on replica sync-depth so a failover is anticipated rather than discovered at repair time, and make the node-drain/OOM/network-event path observable (the precursor for this failover could not be found in the record).
recommended_actions.rationale: The 13:22:10Z failure had no observed external precursor and the historical search for one timed out (gap); an earlier signal would let operators intervene before the empty-replica promotion occurs.

data_gaps: All redis-cache and market-data-service metrics were permanently unavailable (circuit_open: 'query_metrics failed 3 times in a row'): redis-cache cache_hit_rate, command_latency_ms, memory_pct, evicted_keys; pricing-engine and market-data-service request_rate; market-data-service latency_p99_ms (F20, F23, F24). Consequence: the hit-rate collapse could not be measured numerically, and the H1-vs-H2 discriminator (flat vs rising request_rate) can never be tested - H2 can only be weakened, not refuted.

The market-data-service latency samples are log-derived and sparse (3 entries, all from 13:25:19Z onward), with no sample before the first deadline error at 13:23:57Z (F22). Consequence: 'market-data-service was slow before/independent of pricing-engine's timeouts' is inferred, not established.

Onset is bracketed only to the 240s bucket 13:16-13:20Z / 13:16-13:24Z because a fine-grained (30-60s) re-query failed with circuit_open (F8). Consequence: exact minute of the step-change is unknown, so the precedence of the 13:22:10Z failover over the first degraded bucket is inferential.

The precursor search for the redis-cache primary failure (manual drain, memory-limit OOM kill, node maintenance, network event) timed out after 3 attempts (search_historical_incidents ok=false). Consequence: whether the 13:22:10Z failure was spontaneous or caused by an upstream infra action is unobserved.

order-service (upstream caller of pricing-engine) logs could not be retrieved (timeout, 3 attempts). Consequence: upstream blast radius from the caller side is unconfirmed, and the 2-3s reported app latency cannot be reconciled against pricing-engine's p99.

pricing-engine memory_pct was unavailable (timeout, then budget exhausted) and no GC/thread/connection-pool metrics exist. Consequence: memory pressure, GC, or pool exhaustion as an alternative pricing-engine-local mechanism cannot be assessed.

The pricing-engine ERROR log result was truncated (20 of 192 entries returned) and only the market-data-service deadline pattern was visible; a second distinct error signature among the unreturned entries cannot be ruled out.

Off-path consumer logs (auth-service, portfolio-service) are extremely sparse (3-4 lines per 20 minutes) and have no consistent pre-onset p50 baseline, and no metric (hit-rate, connection count) could be consulted for them. Consequence: the 'shared blast radius' claim is weak-positive at best; a brief or low-rate off-path anomaly, or a quote:*-scoped cold set, cannot be excluded.

A second historical-incident search ('cache latency redis shared datastore timeouts') failed with backend unavailable (503). Consequence: the precedent set is limited to the first query's hits and may miss cache-specific precedents.

redis-cache emits no numeric hit/miss/keyspace/dataset-size log line at all (F38, F40, F43). Consequence: the magnitude and exact start of the hit-rate drop cannot be quantified from either logs or metrics.

Deployment history was enumerated window-wide with a successful retry but redis-cache and pricing-engine were not each separately enumerated beyond that; residual risk of a missed per-service deployment is low but non-zero.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Metric evidence showing market-data-service latency_p99_ms was already elevated BEFORE 13:22:10Z (i.e. before the redis-cache failover), which would move the origin upstream of the cache failover and break H1's ordering.

Evidence that the promoted replica redis-cache-3 in fact retained a populated dataset (or that the 'dataset is empty' WARN misreported), which would remove the cold-cache mechanism driving the miss storm and the pricing-engine deadlines.

Evidence that redis-cache request volume (or pricing-engine/market-data-service request_rate) rose sharply in the 13:20Z bucket, which would revive H2 (load surge / capacity saturation) as the onset mechanism.

redis-cache memory_pct at or near its limit with high evicted_keys in the 13:16-13:22Z window, which would indicate eviction/resource exhaustion rather than an empty-replica promotion (F24's unmeasured discriminator).

A redis-cache failover, drain, OOM-kill, or node-maintenance event into the record that clearly precedes and explains the 13:22:10Z PING timeouts, which would relocate the root cause to the upstream infrastructure action rather than the promotion itself.

Repeated evidence on other, non-quote-path redis-cache consumers (auth-service, portfolio-service) of cache-miss/reconnect degradation at ~13:22Z, which would strengthen the 'shared cache-wide' framing (or, conversely, continued clean off-path logs with denser sampling would support a quote:*-scoped cold set instead).

Discovery of a second, distinct pricing-engine ERROR signature (in the truncated 172 unreturned entries) pointing at a different downstream dependency, which would compete with the market-data-service attribution.
A deployment or config change on redis-cache, market-data-service, or pricing-engine in the incident window that the deployment queries missed, which would reopen the change-triggered hypotheses.

findings.statement: Across ALL services in the 11:00-14:00Z window, the only deployment recorded is dep-5604 (auth-service v7.2.0, 'Session cookie hardening', SameSite=strict) at 2026-04-09T11:30:00Z, status 'live', rolled_back_at null. A retry (tc-008, partial=false) confirmed the same single record, so no deployment to pricing-engine appears in this window.

No config changes were recorded for any service in 11:00-14:00Z (count 0, partial=false); a scoped query for redis-cache config changes also returned count 0. The reported change surface in this window is a single auth-service deployment with no rollback.

pricing-engine's dependency graph (depth 2, both directions): downstream to market-data-service (http) and redis-cache (cache); market-data-service also uses redis-cache (cache) and exchange-gateway (http); upstream callers are order-service (http) -> pricing-engine, with api-gateway -> order-service. redis-cache is the only node flagged shared=true and is on the quote path via both pricing-engine and market-data-service.

market-data-service (the direct downstream http dependency of pricing-engine) had zero deployments in a wide 06:00-14:59Z window (count 0, partial=false), so no release of that neighbour coincides with the quote slowdown.

Historical precedents returned for pricing-engine/quote-latency symptoms: HIST-113 (2026-01-28, pricing-engine CPU saturation at market open, root cause 'Record market-open volume exceeded provisioned capacity', category capacity_saturation) and HIST-107 (2025-12-09, 'Cold cache storm after redis failover' on redis-cache/market-data-service, root cause 'Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica', category infrastructure_failure). Lower-match precedents: HIST-101 (auth-service release raised bcrypt cost 10->14, bad_deployment, 'Rolled back v6.4.0') and HIST-110 (order-service/ledger-db IOPS throttling, statement timeouts). These are leads only, not evidence about INC-006.

findings.statement: The auth-service deployment dep-5604 landed at 11:30:00Z, roughly 2 hours before the 13:30Z report, and auth-service does not appear as an upstream caller or downstream dependency of pricing-engine in the depth-2 dependency graph - so this change is not on the retrieved quote path (inference from graph topology, not a causal claim).

pricing-engine p99 latency shows a step-change, not a gradual rise: stable ~60ms through the bucket starting 13:16:00Z (avg 60.33, max 62.93), then the next bucket at 13:20:00Z jumps to avg 1143.04 / max 2227.82ms, and stays ~1.9-2.3s through mid-afternoon before decaying toward ~1.16s.

Metric bucket resolution is 240s for latency_p99_ms, so the exact onset lies between the 13:16:00Z bucket and the 13:20:00Z bucket; the error logs independently place the first timeout at 13:23:57Z. The 13:20:00Z bucket's max of 2227.82ms is already >2s while its avg is 1143.04ms, consistent with onset partway through that 4-minute bucket.

The only ERROR signature on pricing-engine in 12:00-14:59 is timeouts attributed to the downstream dependency market-data-service: 192 matched ERROR entries, all pattern 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms', from 13:23:57Z to 14:58:47Z, with individual cases up to 8456ms.

findings.statement: pricing-engine error rate also step-changed at the same 13:20:00Z bucket: ~0.18-0.24% through 13:16Z, then 2.71% (max 4.23) at 13:20:00Z and a sustained ~4% thereafter (min 0.1, max 4.5).

pricing-engine CPU is NOT elevated during the incident: cpu_pct stays flat at ~38.96-40.59% avg across all buckets 12:00-14:59 (max 44.48), including the onset bucket 13:24:00Z (avg 39.98). This argues against local CPU saturation on pricing-engine as the mechanism.

The latency degradation is temporally coincident across the measured pricing-engine signals: latency p99 and error_rate both step at the 13:20:00Z bucket, and the first market-data-service deadline-exceeded log is 13:23:57Z — consistent with a common onset in the 13:17-13:24Z window.

redis-cache experienced a primary failure/failover at 13:22Z that promoted an EMPTY replica: ERROR 'node redis-cache-2 failed health check (3 consecutive PING timeouts); marking primary as down' at 2026-04-09T13:22:10Z, then WARN 'failover: promoting replica redis-cache-3 to primary; dataset on new primary is empty (replica was resyncing)' at 13:22:52Z.

findings.statement: market-data-service logged a cache-miss storm reading quotes from redis-cache: 289 WARNs of pattern 'cache miss storm: quote:<n> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot (<n>ms)', with first_seen 2026-04-09T13:22:25Z and individual rebuilds of 1034ms-8748ms — matching the 2-3s added latency window reported.

findings.statement: The redis-cache failover (13:22:10Z) precedes market-data-service's cache-miss storm (13:22:25Z) and pricing-engine's first market-data-service deadline-exceeded ERROR (13:23:57Z from T1), placing the dependency-chain onset at ~13:22Z, just before pricing-engine's 13:20Z-bucket p99 step to ~2.2s.

redis-cache then suffered a client reconnect storm indicative of a degraded/recovering primary: WARNs 'client reconnect storm: 15048 new connections in 10s' at 13:30:20Z and 'client reconnect storm: 92851 new connections in 10s' at 13:40:15Z, plus two 'MASTER <-> REPLICA sync started (full resync)' events (13:28:42Z, 13:35:26Z).

findings.statement: Addressing T2's change list: neither auth-service dep-5604 nor market-data-service-failover explanations align with the 13:20Z step-change. The only deployment (dep-5604, auth-service v7.2.0 at 11:30Z) is ~1h50m before onset and off the quote path (F3/F6), and market-data-service had zero deployments in 06:00-14:59Z; the timing evidence points instead to the redis-cache failover at ~13:22Z as the trigger on the quote path.

api-gateway logs are essentially clean across the incident (only 2 WARNs in 12:00-14:59Z: a 12:33:24Z slow /internal/metrics request and a 13:39:42Z 38ms clock-drift NTP resync), showing no independent anomaly or loader signal at the gateway layer.

findings.statement: Pre-incident redis-cache logs (11:00-12:30Z) show no failover, error, or reconnect activity — only an 11:00:37Z deprecated-TLS-cipher WARN and a 12:21:21Z slow /internal/metrics WARN — confirming the failover is a new event starting at 13:22Z, not a pre-existing condition.

findings.statement: The entire consolidated metric probe was blocked: all seven metric queries (redis-cache cache_hit_rate, command_latency_ms, memory_pct, evicted_keys; pricing-engine request_rate; market-data-service request_rate and latency_p99_ms) returned error type 'circuit_open' with the message 'query_metrics failed 3 times in a row; circuit open -- treat this data source as unavailable and record the gap' (retryable=false, attempts=0). No breaker had closed, so the market-data-service latency_p99_ms retry could not be attempted either.
findings.verification_note: 2/3 refs verified (tc-036: quote too short to verify)

findings.statement: market-data-service's own serving latency IS elevated on the quote path during the incident: three INFO log lines 'served batch of requests, p50=<n>ms' show p50=364ms (13:25:19Z), p50=269ms (13:38:45Z), p50=372ms (13:47:18Z). A p50 of ~270-370ms is far above the ~60ms p99 baseline established for pricing-engine pre-onset, i.e. the neighbour service was itself slow across 13:25-13:47Z (log-derived, only 3 samples, not the metric p99).

The market-data-service p50 samples do NOT precede the first deadline error: the earliest is 13:25:19Z, which is ~82s AFTER pricing-engine's first 'market-data-service took <n>ms' deadline ERROR at 13:23:57Z (F9) and after the redis-cache failover at 13:22:10Z (F13). So the log evidence confirms market-data-service was slow, but does not by itself establish its latency was elevated BEFORE 13:23:57Z.

The requested load-surge test (H1 vs H2 on request_rate) could not be performed: pricing-engine and market-data-service request_rate for 12:30-14:00Z both failed circuit_open, so whether request_rate was flat across the 13:20Z step (favoring H1) or sharply rising (reviving H2) is UNANSWERED. No flat-vs-rising determination can be made from metrics.

The redis-cache cold-cache mechanism check is incomplete: cache_hit_rate, command_latency_ms, memory_pct and evicted/expired-key counts were all unavailable (circuit_open). However, the redis-cache failover context already established independently (F13: empty-replica promotion at 13:22:10Z) and the 289-line market-data-service 'cache miss storm ... rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot' WARNs (F14) are the log-side equivalent of a hit-rate collapse, consistent with a cold-cache storm rather than a memory/eviction condition. The memory_pct vs eviction discriminator remains unmeasured.

H2 (pricing-engine capacity saturation / traffic surge) is not supported by any metric retrieved, because none could be retrieved; the only usable negative evidence against H2 remains the already-established flat pricing-engine cpu_pct ~39-40% (F11) and the single off-path deployment (F1/F6). No new metric evidence for or against a load surge was obtained in this round.

redis-cache has ZERO deployments in multiple independent windows: 12:00-14:00Z (count 0) and a wide 2026-04-09T00:00:00Z-14:59:00Z window (count 0). This is the first per-service deployment history ever pulled for redis-cache and it is empty, so redis-cache itself was not changed by any release anywhere on 2026-04-09.
redis-cache also has ZERO config/flag changes in 12:00-14:00Z (count 0), reconfirming F2's scoped result and extending it: no configuration surface on redis-cache changed in the incident window.

Full enumeration of redis-cache consumers from the dependency graph: four services write/read it as kind='cache' — auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service. redis-cache is flagged shared=true, type='redis', owner='platform'. Notably order-service is NOT a direct redis-cache consumer (it reaches the quote path only via http -> pricing-engine), so order-service is not a valid test of redis-cache blast radius at the cache edge.
findings.verification_note: 2/3 refs verified (tc-027: quote not found in tool output)

findings.statement: Two of those consumers are entirely OFF the quote path: auth-service and portfolio-service both consume redis-cache (kind='cache') but sit on api-gateway branches (api-gateway->auth-service, api-gateway->portfolio-service) disjoint from the pricing-engine/market-data-service quote chain. They are therefore the cleanest available blast-radius test for a shared redis-cache origin: if they degraded at ~13:22Z the effect is cache-wide, not quote-path-local.

Neither order-service (count 0) nor portfolio-service (count 0) recorded any deployment in 12:00-14:59Z, so no consumer of redis-cache received a release during the incident window. This rules out a consumer-side deployment as the source of a shared blast radius at 13:22Z.

Historical precedent search for the failover-precursor question returned HIST-107 'Cold cache storm after redis failover' (2025-12-09, services redis-cache + market-data-service, root_cause 'Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica', category infrastructure_failure, match_score 8) — the same mechanism and same two services as the 13:22Z event. The search returned no precedent describing an EXTERNAL precursor (manual drain / OOM kill / node or network event) for a redis primary failure, so the record offers no prior example of a redis failover preceded by an upstream infra action — a lead only, not evidence about INC-006.

findings.statement: auth-service produced ZERO WARN/ERROR log lines in the incident window 13:15-13:35Z (total_matched 0, partial=false, source data_range 09:00-14:59Z i.e. the source is available, not exhausted). The only three entries were INFO: 'connection pool stats: healthy' (13:18:39Z), 'served batch of requests, p50=382ms' (13:24:37Z), 'scheduled job heartbeat ok' (13:27:59Z). No error, latency-error, hit/miss or reconnect anomaly.

portfolio-service produced ZERO WARN/ERROR log lines in 13:15-13:35Z (total_matched 0, attempts=2, partial=false). Its only entries were INFO: 'scheduled job heartbeat ok' (13:15:17Z) and three 'health check ok' at 13:22:32Z, 13:27:51Z and 13:31:20Z — the first of these lands 22s AFTER the redis-cache failover at 13:22:10Z and still reports healthy.

Widening both consumers to 12:00-14:59Z confirms no incident-correlated WARN burst and no reconnect/hit-miss signature: auth-service had exactly 2 WARNs total ('retrying idempotent request (attempt 2) after connection reset' at 12:39:40Z — pre-onset — and 'deprecated TLS cipher offered by client' at 13:11:07Z), and portfolio-service had exactly 3 WARNs (connection-reset retry 12:36:21Z, clock-drift NTP resyncs at 12:52:12Z and 13:50:17Z). None mention redis-cache, cache miss, or failover.

findings.statement: The only latency numbers available for the two off-path consumers are 'served batch of requests, p50=<n>ms' INFO lines, and they show no ~13:22Z step change: auth-service p50=382ms at 13:24:37Z persisting at p50=339ms (13:54:40Z), 445ms (14:11:49Z), 364ms (14:16:00Z); portfolio-service p50=412ms at 13:35:31Z. These are elevated relative to pricing-engine's pre-onset ~60ms p99 baseline but are flat/moderate rather than a degrading-then-recovering incident signature.

Both off-path consumers are demonstrably alive and emitting logs during the test window (auth-service first_match 13:18:39Z / last_match 13:27:59Z; portfolio-service first_match 13:15:17Z / last_match 13:31:20Z), so the zero-WARN result is a genuine clean absence at the log level rather than a silent/absent service — the deciding caveat being that with only ~3-4 log lines per service in 20 minutes the sample is very sparse.

Blast-radius verdict from logs: the redis-cache failover at 13:22:10Z produced visible degradation ONLY on the quote path (market-data-service cache-miss storm from 13:22:25Z, pricing-engine deadline errors from 13:23:57Z), while the two off-path redis-cache consumers on the api-gateway->auth-service and api-gateway->portfolio-service branches show no error/reconnect/hit-miss signature at ~13:22Z — so the 'shared cache-wide blast radius' framing is not supported by the off-path consumers' logs.

redis-cache logs in 13:20-13:30Z contain no hit/miss or keyspace/hit-rate wording: a case-insensitive filter for 'hit' returned total_matched=0, 'keyspace' returned 0, 'miss' returned 0, and 'load' returned 0. The redis-cache log source has no cache_hit_rate-equivalent.

The one hit-rate-adjacent log line in the window is the promotion WARN at 13:22:52Z: 'failover: promoting replica redis-cache-3 to primary; dataset on new primary is empty (replica was resyncing)' — an explicit statement that the newly promoted primary's dataset was empty, i.e. a cold cache at that instant.

dataset on new primary is empty (replica was resyncing)

findings.statement: The complete redis-cache logset for 13:20-13:30Z is only 4 entries (1 ERROR, 2 WARN, 1 INFO): the 13:22:10Z primary-down ERROR, the 13:22:52Z empty-replica promotion WARN, a 13:28:15Z 'background saving terminated with success' INFO, and a 13:28:42Z 'MASTER <-> REPLICA sync started (full resync)' WARN — no per-request keyspace/hit counters are emitted by this service at all.

Pre-onset baseline shows redis-cache was actively persisting and healthy-normal right up to 13:18:40Z with NO hit-rate/keyspace wording: 9 INFO lines in 12:30-13:22Z, all 'background saving terminated with success' (6) or '<n> changes in <n> seconds. Saving...' (3); the last pre-failover line is 13:18:40Z. This confirms the failover (13:22:10Z) is the boundary and no cache-metric-style line precedes it.

The only redis-cache signal that can delimit a POST-13:22Z-only degradation is the failover event itself, which is not present before 13:22:10Z: the 13:20-13:30Z window's first match is 13:22:10Z and no failover/empty/keyspace wording appears in the 12:30-13:22Z baseline, so any cache-hit degradation is bounded to after 13:22:10Z by construction of the log evidence.

The redis-cache log source cannot supply a hit-rate time series and is effectively exhausted for this question: every targeted keyword ('hit', 'keyspace', 'miss', 'load') returned total_matched=0, and the unfiltered all-level pulls (tc-043, tc-055) return only lifecycle/persistence events. The log-side equivalent of cache_hit_rate therefore does not exist; the miss-side must be read from the consumer (market-data-service, F14).
